extracted.intended_audience: IP practitioners, in-house counsel, businesses and foreign counsel seeking an overview of Philippine intellectual property law
extracted.subtask_description: A jurisdictional Q&A summarizing Philippine intellectual property laws, rights, registration procedures, durations, ownership rules, oppositions, remedies and enforcement for patents, utility models, industrial designs, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, layout-designs and geographical indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any technical solution of a problem in any field of human activity which is (1) new, (2) involves an inventive step, and (3) is industrially applicable shall be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent is an exclusive right granted in exchange for full disclosure. Patent owner may restrain, prohibit and prevent unauthorized persons from making, using, offering for sale, selling or importing the patented product, or using the patented process; may assign and license the patent and commence infringement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent rights and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner has the right to prevent unauthorized making, using, offering for sale, selling or importing of the patented product, or use of the patented process; may assign or license the patent and commence an infringement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court remedies include damages, injunctive writs, orders for disposal of infringing goods/materials/implements without compensation; repeated infringement can trigger criminal liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility models protect inventions which are new and industrially applicable; these inventions do not need to have an inventive step, unlike a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility model holders enjoy protections similar to patent owners. Utility model registration right belongs to the person who filed the application; where multiple applications exist for same subject, earliest filing/priority date controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model duration and conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model is protected for a non-renewable period of seven (7) years from the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At any time before grant or refusal, an applicant for a patent may convert to utility model registration (and vice versa) upon payment of prescribed fee; an application may only be converted once; cannot file two applications (patent & utility model) for same subject — only earliest filing considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design registrability and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design refers to any composition of lines or colors or any three-dimensional form, whether or not associated with lines or colors, provided it gives a special appearance to and can serve as pattern for an industrial product or handicraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs dictated essentially by technical or functional considerations to obtain a technical result or those contrary to public order, health or morals are not protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design rights and term
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial design owners enjoy the same rights conferred to a patent owner, including bringing infringement actions for making, using, offering for sale, selling, or importing a product using the registered design without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term of protection is five (5) years from filing, renewable for up to two consecutive five-year periods (maximum total 15 years) upon payment of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout-design (topography) eligibility and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout-design of an integrated circuit refers to a three-dimensional disposition of elements (at least one active element) and interconnections; a layout-design is original if it is the result of its creator’s own intellectual effort and is not commonplace among creators/manufacturers at the time of creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner has rights to reproduce and commercialize the layout-design subject to originality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout-design rights limitations and term
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner cannot prevent third parties from reproducing, selling or distributing the registered layout-design in certain circumstances (private use, evaluation/research/teaching, where act performed on independently created original layout-design, or where the registered layout-design or article has been put on the market by or with consent of the right holder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration valid for ten (10) years without renewal. Specific rules apply for persons who acquired article unaware of unlawful reproduction; liability limited to stock on hand after notice with minimum royalty of 5% of net sales or reasonable royalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrability and exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark registration gives the owner the exclusive right to make use of the mark and prevent others from using the same or similar marks on identical or related goods or services where such use would result in a likelihood of confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of an identical sign for identical goods/services gives a presumption of likelihood of confusion. Registration confers legal presumption of ownership; the registrant in good faith is owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-known marks and unfair competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection of a well-known mark shall extend to goods and services which are not similar if use would indicate a connection between those goods/services and the owner and the interests of the owner are likely to be damaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfair competition elements: (1) passing off goods/business/services for those of another with established goodwill; and (2) intent to deceive the public, defraud a competitor, or act contrary to good faith. Unregistered but well-known marks may bring actions for unfair competition if they have sufficient goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark term, renewal and use requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark is protected for ten (10) years from approval of registration and can be renewed indefinitely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner must file a Declaration of Actual Use (DAU) within three (3) years from filing date and within one (1) year from the fifth anniversary of registration; renewal requests may be made within six months before expiry or within six months after expiry with surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright subject matter and economic rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright protects original literary, artistic, and scientific works, including books, music, paintings, and computer programs. Economic rights include: (a) reproduction; (b) dramatization/translation/adaptation/arrangement; (c) first public distribution; (d) rental of originals/copies of certain works; (e) public display; (f) public performance; and (g) other communication to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic rights confer exclusive rights to carry out, authorize or prevent those acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral rights and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral rights arise automatically: (a) right of attribution; (b) right to make alterations or to withhold publication; (c) right to object to distortion/mutilation/modification prejudicial to honour or reputation; (d) right to restrain use of name with respect to work not of his creation or in distorted version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An author can waive moral rights by written instrument pursuant to the IP Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright duration and registration effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright protection lasts for the lifetime of the author and fifty (50) years after the author's death (for joint authorship, life of last surviving author plus 50 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright arises upon creation; registration is not essential but depositing the work with National Library or IPOPHL provides a certificate as prima facie evidence of ownership. Registration process is generally completed within weeks to a few months; Certificate of Registration released within seven working days when documents complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade secret definition, protection and non-registrability
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade secrets are information (formulas, processes, methods) giving competitive advantage and kept confidential. They are protected as long as they remain confidential and provide a competitive advantage and are not registrable rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection commonly via confidentiality agreements/NDAs; also protected under general criminal law (e.g., Article 291 RPC), tax law, corporate rehabilitation rules, and environmental statutes where confidentiality is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indications eligibility and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical indications identify a good as originating from a specific place where a particular quality, reputation or characteristic is attributed to its geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant may prevent misleading acts suggesting false origin. Registration may be filed by producers, government agencies/local government units, organizations or indigenous cultural communities. Registered GI is protected for an unlimited term unless revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration terms for each IP right
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified protection periods: patents 20 years from filing (non-renewable); utility models 7 years (non-renewable); industrial designs 5 years initial, renewable twice (max 15 years); layout-design registrations 10 years (no renewal); trademarks 10 years renewable indefinitely; copyrights life +50 years; geographical indications protected while used and reputation maintained or until revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent term subject to annual fees; rules differ for commencement of layout-design protection (first commercial exploitation or filing date if not previously exploited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply / initial ownership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents/utility models: right belongs to inventor(s), heirs or assigns; applications may be filed by inventor(s) or in the name of heirs/legal representatives/assignees. Trademarks: natural or juridical persons may apply. Copyright: author or creator (or heir/assignee) may apply for certificate of registration. Geographical indications: producers/government/local units/organizations/indigenous communities may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership rules: first-to-file rule applies for patents; inventorship not automatically ownership. For employment: if inventive activity is not part of regular duties, patent belongs to employee; if part of regular duties, patent belongs to employer. Commissioned works generally belong to commissioner unless contract provides otherwise. Registrant in good faith is owner of trademark; industrial design/layout-design ownership acquired through registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent/utility model/industrial design registration procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: General procedural steps: filing application with required information (title, specification, claims, abstract, drawings), payment of filing/publication fees, IPOPHL initial/formality examination, search for prior art, publication (generally after 18 months for patents), (upon request) substantive examination, and grant upon meeting statutory/regulatory requirements and payment of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics vary by IP type (utility model similar but registration certificate granted rather than patent grant; industrial designs and layout-designs have formality and registrability checks and publication in IPOPHL E-Gazette).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination, publication and substantive examination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications are published after 18 months from filing or priority date unless otherwise allowed; substantive examination is by request to determine patentability. Industrial design and layout-design may be published after formality examination; IPOPHL conducts searches for prior art for registrability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPOPHL will release Registrability Reports for trademarks and GIs; deficiencies must be remedied within prescribed periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical time-to-grant: patents generally take 3–5 years; utility models/industrial designs/layout-designs typically 6 months to one year; trademarks typically 6 months to one year after application; geographical indications 6 months to one year; copyright registration several weeks to a few months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variances depend on office actions, responses, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party participation and opposition windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may present observations on patents after publication. For trademarks, a 30-day publication period allows any party who may be damaged to file an opposition. For geographical indications, notice of third-party observation may be filed within one (1) month from publication. For voluntary withdrawal of utility model registration, any person prejudiced may present a written Opposition within 15 days from publication of declaration of withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition proceedings are inter partes and governed by IPOPHL Rules; Bureau of Legal Affairs serves notices and sets hearings for trademark oppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and new matter restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend a patent application during examination; amendment shall not include new matter outside the scope of the disclosure contained in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after official action, applicant presents claims directed to an invention divisible from previously claimed invention, such claims if entered will be refused and applicant required to limit claims to the invention previously claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion and prohibition on duplicate filings
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time before grant or refusal, an applicant may convert between patent and utility model applications (conversion grants filing date of initial application); an application may be converted only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may not file two applications for the same subject (one for utility model and one for patent) whether simultaneously or consecutively; where multiple applications exist, only earliest filing/priority date is considered and others deemed forfeited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on rights and non-excludable acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain acts are permitted despite registration: e.g., layout-design owner cannot prevent reproduction for private purposes or solely for evaluation, analysis, research or teaching; reproductions based on such analysis that are original are permitted; acts on articles put on the market by or with consent of right holder are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In integrated circuits, persons acquiring the article without reasonable ground to know of unlawful reproduction may continue to perform acts on stock on hand until notified, but after notice liability applies to subsequent acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and timing for revocation/cancellation/invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for invalidity include failure to meet statutory requirements (e.g., lack of novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability for patents), fraudulent procurement, genericness, non-fulfillment of GI protection conditions, change in geographical origin that disqualifies GI, lack of effective control for GI, or non-use of a mark in the Philippines for three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition and cancellation remedies have various time-limits: trademark opposition within 30 days of publication; cancellation generally within five years of registration (but certain grounds may be raised at any time); GI third-party observation within one month; patent-related court action must be filed within one year from date of publication of patent application (IP Code reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum and procedures for challenge and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent court actions are instituted before Regional Trial Courts designated as Special Commercial Courts. Oppositions and cancellations for trademarks and other IP administrative proceedings may be brought before the Bureau of Legal Affairs. Criminal complaints proceed via Department of Justice/Prosecutor then to appropriate court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes administrative proceedings are governed by IPOPHL rules. Civil actions commence by verified complaint; appeals taken to Court of Appeals under Rules of Court; criminal case procedures include arraignment, pre-trial (terminated within 30 days), mediation referral, expedited hearings and judgment within 60 days of submission for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for infringement across IP types
rubrics_metrics.description: Available remedies include civil damages, injunctive writs, impounding and destruction of infringing goods/devices without compensation, delivery/disposal, and criminal actions for repeated or egregious infringement; administrative remedies and provisional measures are available at IPOPHL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark damages may be doubled if intentional mislead; administrative remedies may grant temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctions, preliminary attachment. For trade secrets, injunction and criminal prosecution (e.g., revelation of industrial secrets) are available. For copyright, statutory damages, injunctive relief, impounding, destruction and criminal/administrative remedies exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs, bonds and security for enforcement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Various fees apply for IPO inter partes cases and administrative complaints. A bond is required for issuance of writs of search and seizure or motions for disposal/destruction, conditioned to compensate damages the defendant may sustain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney’s fees and litigation expenses are normally incurred and can be recovered in a favorable civil judgment. Specific fee schedules are provided in IPOPHL memoranda and rules.
